facts.content: Patient has a cough and cold for 5 days.
Patient reports a dry, hacking cough, runny nose (rhinorrhea), muscle aches (myalgias), intermittent headaches, and chills.
facts.source_text: Dry, hacking cough; rhinorrhea; myalgias; intermittent HA; chills

facts.content: Patient denies shortness of breath or wheezing and reports no rattly chest noises.
facts.source_text: Denies SOB/wheeze; no rattly chest noises

facts.content: Patient denies swelling of neck glands.
Patient has a history of diabetes mellitus for approximately 5 to 6 years.
Patient has a history of hypertension.
Mild posterior erythema in oropharynx; tonsils not enlarged.
facts.source_text: OP: mild posterior erythema; tonsils not enlarged

facts.content: No palpable glands in the neck as per the patient.
The assessment is a viral upper respiratory tract infection with a dry cough for 5 days, rhinorrhea, myalgias, headache, chills, no shortness of breath or wheezing, and a benign oropharyngeal exam.
facts.source_text: Viral URTI with dry cough ×5 d; rhinorrhea/myalgias/HA/chills; no SOB/wheeze; benign OP exam.

facts.content: Symptomatic treatment advised with Day Nurse or Night Nurse over-the-counter medications, which are acceptable with current medications.
facts.source_text: Symptomatic tx: Day Nurse/Night Nurse OTC acceptable with current meds

facts.content: Safety net advice given to seek care if shortness of breath, wheezing, condition worsening, or symptoms persist for more than 3 weeks; may need chest exam.
facts.source_text: Safety-net: seek care if SOB, wheeze, worsening, or sx >3 wks; may need chest exam
